stem:
For a school science exhibition, Meera wraps 40 turns of insulated copper wire around an iron nail and connects the ends to a dry cell. When the current flows, the nail picks up several steel paper clips. When she disconnects the cell, the clips fall off.
What do these observations show?

options.text: The coil acts as a temporary magnet only while current flows, and the iron nail makes the electromagnet stronger.
The coil acts as a permanent magnet, and the iron nail makes the electromagnet weaker.
The coil cannot act as a magnet unless the iron nail inside it heats up first.
The iron nail becomes a permanent magnet and keeps attracting the clips even without current.

teacher.key_rationale: A current-carrying coil behaves like a magnet; an iron core strengthens the electromagnet; when current stops the magnetism is lost (clips fall), so the magnetism is temporary. B wrongly claims weaker/permanent, C adds a heating condition not required, D claims permanent magnetism contradicted by the clips falling.
